clips.send: Carthage (near Tunis). A Phoenician trading city in North Africa and Rome’s great rival. Rome fought it in three Punic Wars (264–146 BCE) and destroyed it in 146 BCE; Romans later rebuilt it as a Roman city.

clips.send: Syracuse. A rich Greek colony on Sicily, founded by Corinth about 733 BCE. Home of the mathematician Archimedes (died 212 BCE).

clips.send: Rome. Legend says Rome was founded in 753 BCE on seven hills by the Tiber River. Republic from 509 BCE, Empire from 27 BCE; about a million people lived here around 1 CE (estimate).

clips.send: Olympia. Site of the ancient Olympic Games, held every four years for Zeus from 776 BCE. During the games a truce let athletes travel safely.

clips.send: Coloured areas show who ruled where in the year on the slider. Borders are rough — ancient empires had no exact lines on the ground. Pericles: Leader of Athens in its golden age; paid citizens for public service and built the Parthenon. Socrates, Plato, Aristotle: Three Athenian philosophers: teacher, student, student. Aristotle then taught Alexander. Alexander the Great: King of Macedon (336–323 BCE); conquered from Greece to the Indus River and spread Greek culture. Hannibal: Carthaginian general who crossed the Alps with elephants in 218 BCE. Julius Caesar: Conquered Gaul, became dictator, was killed in 44 BCE. Augustus (Octavian): First Roman emperor (27 BCE – 14 CE); began two centuries of “Roman Peace” (Pax Romana).

clips.send: Athens. The leading sea power of Greece and birthplace of democracy (reforms of Solon 594 BCE and Cleisthenes 508 BCE). Under Pericles (about 461–429 BCE) it built the Parthenon and led the Delian League.

clips.send: 彩色区域表示滑块所示年份时各国统治的范围。疆界只是大致范围——古代帝国并没有精确的边界线。 伯里克利：雅典黄金时代的领导人，给担任公职的公民发津贴，主持修建帕特农神庙。 苏格拉底、柏拉图、亚里士多德：三位雅典哲学家，一代传一代；亚里士多德后来又当了亚历山大的老师。 亚历山大大帝：马其顿国王（前336—前323年在位），征服了从希腊到印度河的广大地区，传播了希腊文化。 汉尼拔：迦太基名将，前218年带着战象翻越阿尔卑斯山。 恺撒：征服高卢，成为独裁官，前44年遇刺身亡。 屋大维（奥古斯都）：罗马第一位皇帝（前27—公元14年在位），开启了约两百年的“罗马和平”。

clips.send: 迦太基（今突尼斯附近）。北非的腓尼基人商业城市，罗马的强劲对手。罗马与它进行了三次布匿战争（前264—前146年），前146年将其摧毁；后来罗马人又在原址重建城市。
